product_family: Developer-first open-source supply chain security platform: Socket CLI and GitHub App/Action for dependency risk scanning (npm, PyPI, Go, etc.), Socket Firewall (registry-level malware interception, self-hosted or client/server), and Socket Firewall Enterprise (org-wide policy enforcement). Free for open source; paid Team/Business/Enterprise tiers add SSO/SAML, SCIM, SBOM, and reachability analysis.

privacy.ai_training_note: Socket's security page states the product 'is designed to work without the need to analyze, upload, or share your source code' and that 'the only data we collect from your repository is the manifest files and associated lockfiles such as package-lock.json and yarn.lock.' No vendor-domain statement confirms or denies use of that dependency-manifest data, or any customer data, to train Socket's own risk-scoring/AI models.

top_certs: SOC 2 Type II (2023 attestation; current status not reconfirmed on vendor's live security page)

flags: Socket's own blog announced a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation in February 2023, but Socket's current security page (as of 2026-07-09) does not mention SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, or HIPAA under its 'Security Certifications' heading, listing only third-party TLS/configuration scan ratings (Mozilla Observatory, Qualys SSL Labs). This could mean the SOC 2 program lapsed, moved to a private trust-center/NDA process, or the security page is not kept in sync with compliance status. SOC 2 reports are normally re-issued annually, so current validity of the 2023 attestation is not confirmed.

No public trust center (e.g. a Vanta- or Drata-hosted trust page) is published for Socket. Socket integrates with Vanta as a product feature for customers' own compliance programs; this integration is a product capability, not evidence of a Socket-operated trust center.
AI-training posture on customer data is not addressed anywhere on the vendor domain.
